component.name: Apache Axis2 C Core
component.description: SOAP and REST web services engine implemented in C. Provides HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 transports, dual XML parsers (Guththila and libxml2), native JSON processing (json-c), MTOM/XOP attachment handling, and hot-deployment of services. Runs as a standalone HTTP server or as an Apache httpd module (mod_axis2). Being a C implementation, memory safety vulnerabilities are in scope in addition to the logical vulnerabilities shared with Axis2/Java.

externalReferences.comment: Source security model document; this file is a structured translation of it.

blueprints.name: Axis2/C message processing pipeline
blueprints.description: Architecture described by the threat model: a remote client's untrusted input passes through Apache httpd (TLS, connection limits, WAF) or the development-only standalone axis2_http_server, into mod_axis2 / the HTTP request processor, Content-Type routing to a JSON or XML parser, the AXIOM object model, dispatchers, handler phases (where the Rampart/C security module executes), the message receiver invoking the service function, and response serialization.

assets.name: HTTP front end (Apache httpd with mod_axis2, or standalone server)
assets.description: Apache httpd handling TLS, connection limits and WAF for production deployments via mod_axis2; the standalone axis2_http_server is single-threaded, has no production-grade connection limits and is intended for development only. HTTP/2 is provided via nghttp2 (CVE-2023-44487 rapid reset mitigated by the nghttp2 version).

assets.name: XML parsers (Guththila and libxml2)
assets.description: Guththila (default) is inherently XXE-safe (no entity processing) and fuzz-tested via OSS-Fuzz. The optional libxml2 parser is hardened with XML_PARSE_NONET, a custom entity loader blocking all external resolution, a depth limit of 256, an attribute limit of 256, and a namespace limit of 64.

assets.name: JSON parsers (json-c and JSON-to-AXIOM reader)
assets.description: json-c direct parsing on the HTTP/2 path and the JSON-to-AXIOM reader on the HTTP/1.1 path; both fuzz-tested, with a 64-level depth limit and a 10MB payload size limit.

assets.name: HTTP header, request line and MTOM/XOP handling
assets.description: HTTP header formatting uses sprintf() writing to a heap buffer sized from measured input lengths, fuzz-tested via OSS-Fuzz; status line limited to 512 bytes; MTOM/XOP attachments bounded by a 100MB default chunked transfer maximum.

assets.name: HTTP client transport (outbound)
assets.description: Outbound transport with TLS 1.2+ enforced, SSLv2/SSLv3/TLS 1.0-1.1 disabled, AEAD ciphers only, and hostname validation enabled.

assets.name: Services directory and configuration
assets.description: Hot-deployment directory for service shared libraries (.so/.dll) and axis2.xml configuration, writable by the server administrator and service deployers.

zones.name: Remote clients
zones.description: Anonymous clients are untrusted remote callers with no credentials who can reach any HTTP endpoint; all their input is hostile. Authenticated clients (identity verified by TLS client certificate, WS-Security via Rampart/C, or application-level auth) are partially trusted.

zones.name: Axis2/C engine
zones.description: The message processing pipeline: transports, parsers, AXIOM, dispatchers, handler phases and message receivers.

zones.name: Deployment host
zones.description: Filesystem holding axis2.xml, TLS certificates and the services directory, managed by the fully trusted server administrator and trusted service deployers.

persona.description: Fully trusted. Configures axis2.xml, compiles with chosen parser/transport options, manages TLS certificates, deploys services.
Trusted. Deploys shared libraries (.so/.dll) into the services directory; has filesystem write access.
Partially trusted. Identity verified by transport (TLS client cert), WS-Security (via Rampart/C), or application-level auth.
Untrusted remote caller with no credentials. Can reach any HTTP endpoint. All input is hostile.

threats.name: Remote code execution via memory corruption
threats.description: Buffer overflow, format string, or other memory corruption exploitable by a remote attacker through the Axis2/C framework, and memory safety violations (heap/stack buffer overflows, use-after-free, double-free, null pointer dereferences) reachable from untrusted input. The threat model rates buffer overflow, use-after-free, format string, integer overflow and null dereference risks as low after the January 2026 hardening (correctly sized heap allocations, allocator-based memory management with ASAN testing, code review of logging macros, defensive null checks).

threats.name: Integer overflow in size calculations
threats.description: Size calculations in buffer allocation or payload processing that wrap around, leading to undersized buffers and subsequent overflows. Payload size limits prevent wrap-around in allocation; integer overflow and size_t consistency fixes from a Gemini code review were applied in early 2026.

threats.name: Format string vulnerabilities
threats.description: User-controlled data passed as the format argument to printf-family functions or logging macros. Risk rated low: a code review addressed logging macro usage in January 2026, and recommended build flags include -Wformat -Wformat-security.

threats.name: XML External Entity (XXE) injection
threats.description: The XML parser resolves external entities from untrusted input, enabling file read or SSRF. Guththila is inherently immune (no entity processing); libxml2 requires hardening and is configured with XML_PARSE_NONET and a custom entity loader that blocks all external resolution. XXE in WSDL/XSD imported schemas is handled by the chosen XML parser's hardening.

threats.name: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
threats.description: The server makes requests to arbitrary hosts due to attacker-controlled URLs in WSDL imports, external entities, or client-side HTTP transport. URL parsing is fuzz-tested via the fuzz_url_parser OSS-Fuzz target for SSRF detection.

threats.name: Denial of service via parser abuse
threats.description: XML bombs, deeply nested JSON (more than 64 levels), or payloads exceeding size limits (over 10MB) that crash the process or exhaust memory; deep-nesting stack exhaustion in Guththila and the JSON paths; large attachment or temp file exhaustion via MTOM/XOP; recursive schema DoS in WSDL/XSD validation. The document notes there are no explicit limits on schema complexity or recursion depth during WSDL/XSD validation, a potential DoS risk.

threats.name: Information disclosure in faults and error responses
threats.description: Stack traces, internal paths, or configuration details leaked in SOAP faults or HTTP error responses.

threats.name: TLS/SSL vulnerabilities in the client transport
threats.description: Acceptance of deprecated protocols (SSLv2, SSLv3, TLS 1.0/1.1) or weak cipher suites in the HTTP client transport; TLS downgrade and hostname validation bypass. The client transport enforces TLS 1.2+, disables the deprecated protocols, uses AEAD ciphers only and enables hostname validation.

threats.name: HTTP header injection and malformed header parsing
threats.description: Header injection (CRLF) and malformed header parsing against http_header.c, and oversized or malformed request/status lines. Mitigated by heap buffers sized from measured input lengths, a 512-byte status line limit, delimiter-based request line parsing, and OSS-Fuzz coverage.

threats.name: Vulnerabilities in tracked dependencies
threats.description: Known CVE classes in OpenSSL, libxml2, json-c, nghttp2 and Apache httpd (e.g. CVE-2020-12762 integer overflow in json-c, CVE-2023-44487 HTTP/2 rapid reset in nghttp2). The project documents minimum dependency versions and runs monthly CVE checks via GitHub Actions.

threats.name: Vulnerabilities in user-written services
threats.description: Input validation, SQL injection, and business logic flaws in deployed service implementations are the service author's responsibility, not a security issue in Axis2/C.

threats.name: Missing authentication on endpoints
threats.description: Axis2/C does not ship built-in authentication. Securing endpoints is the responsibility of Rampart/C, the web server (Apache httpd), or a reverse proxy. Vulnerabilities in the optional, external Rampart/C (WS-Security) module belong to that separate project.

threats.name: Hot-deployment with weak filesystem permissions
threats.description: If an attacker can write to the services directory, they can deploy arbitrary shared libraries. This is an OS-level access control issue, not an Axis2/C security issue.

threats.name: Denial of service at the network level
threats.description: SYN floods, slowloris, and connection exhaustion are mitigated by Apache httpd or the network infrastructure, not by Axis2/C.

threats.name: Use of the standalone HTTP server in production
threats.description: The standalone axis2_http_server is intended for development/testing: single-threaded, without production-grade connection limits. Production deployments should use mod_axis2 behind a reverse proxy; issues arising only from production use of the standalone server are not security issues.

trustBoundaries.name: HTTP entry trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: Remote clients (anonymous ones untrusted, all input hostile) deliver bytes into the message processing pipeline through Apache httpd/mod_axis2 or the standalone server.

trustBoundaries.name: Deployment trust boundary
trustBoundaries.description: The services directory and axis2.xml are managed by trusted administrators and deployers; write access to the services directory is equivalent to arbitrary code deployment and is protected by OS-level access control.

controls.name: Parser depth and size limits
controls.description: JSON payload size limit (10MB) and depth limit (64 levels); libxml2 depth limit 256, attribute limit 256, namespace limit 64; HTTP status line limit 512 bytes; MTOM chunked transfer maximum 100MB by default; payload size limits preventing integer wrap-around in allocation.

controls.name: XXE-safe XML parsing
controls.description: Guththila performs no entity processing and is inherently XXE-safe; the optional libxml2 parser uses XML_PARSE_NONET and a custom entity loader override that blocks all external entity resolution.

controls.name: TLS 1.2+ with strong ciphers in the client transport
controls.description: TLS 1.0/1.1 completely disabled; SSLv2/SSLv3 disabled; strong cipher suites enforced (AEAD plus forward secrecy); hostname validation enabled.

controls.name: OSS-Fuzz integration
controls.description: Active OSS-Fuzz integration with 5 fuzz targets (fuzz_xml_parser, fuzz_json_parser, fuzz_json_reader, fuzz_http_header, fuzz_url_parser) plus application-level fuzz_finbench testing with integer overflow and boundary value inputs; local fuzzing validated with over 8M iterations and zero ASAN errors.

controls.name: Build-time hardening flags
controls.description: Production builds should use CFLAGS="-fstack-protector-strong -D_FORTIFY_SOURCE=2 -fPIE -Wformat -Wformat-security" and LDFLAGS="-pie -Wl,-z,relro,-z,now"; AddressSanitizer is available for development via --enable-asan.

controls.name: January-February 2026 hardening and feature removals
controls.description: NTLM authentication, the TCP transport, the CGI transport and the libcurl HTTP backend were removed (AXIS2C-1708); TLS 1.0/1.1 disabled; strong cipher suites enforced; JSON limits added; libxml2 entity loader override added; integer overflow and size_t consistency fixes from Gemini code review applied.

controls.name: Dependency minimum versions and CVE monitoring
controls.description: Minimum versions tracked for OpenSSL (1.1.1k+), libxml2 (2.9.10+), json-c (0.15+), nghttp2 (1.50.0+) and Apache httpd (2.4.62+), with monthly CVE checks via a GitHub Actions workflow.

controls.name: Deploy via mod_axis2 behind a reverse proxy
controls.description: Use Apache httpd with mod_axis2 (TLS, connection limits, WAF) behind a reverse proxy in production; the standalone HTTP server is for development only. See docs/SECURITY.md for detailed deployment hardening guidance.
